svg.title: How collate.py turns clean ProstT5Dataset rows into a conditioned training batch
svg.desc: TaskCollator.collate turns a list of B clean ProstT5Dataset rows into one training batch. Two rows are drawn side by side in every card, proteins of 67 and 55 residues on a 70-position canvas, and a faded third column shows that the batch continues. default_collate stacks x [B, 8, 70], seed_3di [B, 70], residue_mask [B, 70], c [B, 3] and dimer_index [B]. Step 1, sample_task_batch in sampling.py, lets each row draw its own task. Row 0 draws the middle layout, keeps the slice [12, 52) in seed_x, lets spans.py cut the hole [27, 34), and makes both ends editable in edit_mask. Its 3Di stays on fixed context and on the two ends, while the hole loses it. Row 1 draws redesign with mode 3di, so seed_x is empty, edit_mask covers the whole canvas including padding, and all 55 3Di tokens stay. Step 2, mask_training_threedi_conditioning in masking.py, runs only in training and hides spans of the remaining 3Di tokens on editable residues, zeroing them in seed_3di and marking them in threedi_conditioning_hidden_mask. Step 3, property_mask in masking.py, builds condition_mask [B, 3]. Row 0 keeps length and hydrophobicity and hides charge; row 1, a 3di redesign, hides all three. The batch then goes to training/step.py, where model_inputs reads seed_x, edit_mask, seed_3di, threedi_conditioning_hidden_mask, c and condition_mask, and compute_loss reads x, edit_mask, residue_mask and target_length.
